Hotel comment: 'I represent a hotel. I know my floors, numbered from the first one, and I am the one guests talk to: they can be received at a floor and room, a room can be reserved for them and they can be received in a room they reserved before. I also know how many of my rooms are available, occupied and reserved, and my profits and losses, which are the sum of the ones of my floors.'.
Floor comment: 'I represent a floor of a Hotel. I know my rooms, numbered from the first one, and the price of each type of guest on me. Guests are received and rooms are reserved through me, so nobody has to reach my rooms to do it. My profits are what my occupied and reserved rooms produce and my losses are what my available rooms cost me.'.
Room comment: 'I represent a room of a Floor. I am available, reserved or occupied by a type of guest, and it is my state, a RoomState, the one that knows what can be done to me and how much profit and loss I produce. Receiving a guest, receiving a guest with a reservation and reserving me leave me in the state my current one answers.'.
RoomState comment: 'I am the state of a Room: available, reserved or occupied. My subclasses know, for the state they represent, whether a guest can be received, whether a guest with a reservation can be received and whether the room can be reserved, answering the state the room is left in and signalling an error when it can not be done. They also know the profit and the loss the room produces with a price list.'.
AvailableRoomState comment: 'I am the state of a Room nobody is in and nobody has reserved. A guest can be received in it and it can be reserved. It produces no profit and its loss is the most expensive price of the list, because that is what the hotel is not earning with it.'.
ReservedRoomState comment: 'I am the state of a Room that was reserved and whose guest has not arrived yet. Only a guest with a reservation can be received in it. It produces half of the cheapest price of the list as profit and no loss.'.
OccupiedRoomState comment: 'I am the state of a Room a guest is in. I know the type of that guest, which is what its profit is looked up with in the price list. No other guest can be received in it and it can not be reserved. It produces no loss.'.
RoomTest comment: 'I test a Room, the states it goes through and the profit and loss it produces.'.
FloorTest comment: 'I test a Floor: how it is created, how guests are received and rooms reserved on it and the profits and losses it produces.'.
HotelTest comment: 'I test a Hotel: how it is created, how guests are received and rooms reserved in it and the profits and losses it produces.'.

All 39 tests pass (78 counted because both categories are run). Here's what changed.

## 1 & 2 — Instantiation of `Floor` and `Hotel`
Replaced the `new` + `setXxx:` pairs with instance-creation funnels that validate on the class side and send a single `initialize…`:

- `Floor class>>#with:roomsPricedBy:` → `assertIsValidNumberOfRooms:`, `assertIsValidPriceList:`, then `initializeWith:roomsPricedBy:`
- `Hotel class>>#withFloors:` → `assertIsValidFloorCollection:`, then `initializeWithFloors:`

`Hotel` lost `availableRoomsCount`: the counter was a cache that `receiveWithReservation:…` never updated, so availability is now asked of the floors.

## 3 & 4 — Room states
`Room` holds a `state` and delegates everything to it. New hierarchy `RoomState` (abstract, `subclassResponsibility`) with `AvailableRoomState`, `ReservedRoomState`, `OccupiedRoomState` (the only one knowing a `guestType`). Each state answers the state the room is left in, so `#receive:`, `#receiveWithReservation:` and `#reserve` are each a single line with no repeated `guest = #reserved` tests, and `nil`/`#reserved` are gone from the model.

## 5, 6 & 7 — Encapsulation and repetition
- `Floor>>#rooms` deleted. `Floor` now answers `#receive:atRoom:`, `#receiveWithReservation:atRoom:`, `#reserveRoom:` on top of a private `#roomAt:`; the three `Hotel` methods are one line each over `#floorAt:`.
- Added `Room>>#lossUsing:ifAbsentGuestType:`, so `Floor>>#totalLosses` is `rooms sum: [...]` just like `#totalProfits` instead of reaching for `prices values max` itself.
- Every `Hotel` total is now `floors sum: [...]` and `#isEmpty` is `floors allSatisfy: [...]`; the `whileTrue:` loops are gone.
- Tests 13, 14 and 15 of `RoomTest` no longer use `#shouldFail:` and pass.
- Fixed `Floor class>>#signalUnknownGuestType`, which sent `self class unknownGuestTypeErrorDescription` from the class side and would have raised a `MessageNotUnderstood` instead of the intended error.

## 8 — Tests
`FloorTest` no longer reaches into `floor rooms`; `HotelTest` gained `#createHotelWithOneFloor` and `#assertNoRoomIsTakenIn:`, which the five error tests share. Test classes moved to `ISW1-2024-1C-Parcial-Tests`, and every class got a real comment in place of the template one.

One thing to flag: **`roomNumberDoesNotExistErrorDescription` moved from `Hotel` to `Floor`**, and the four `HotelTest` methods asserting it now read `Floor roomNumberDoesNotExistErrorDescription`. `Floor` is the one that knows its rooms, and leaving the message on `Hotel` would have made `Floor` depend on `Hotel`. The error text is unchanged. If you would rather the tests keep naming `Hotel`, say so and I'll put it back.
